questions.question: What shape is a hazardous materials placard?
questions.explanation: Vehicles carrying hazardous materials must display diamond-shaped warning signs on all four sides. These signs are called placards.

questions.question: Which agency must check you before you get a HazMat endorsement?
questions.explanation: You must pass a security check by the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) to get a hazardous materials endorsement.

questions.question: If your vehicle carrying Class 1 explosives is in a collision, you should:

options.text: Not warn others of the danger.
Keep the explosives inside the vehicle until after separating the vehicles.
Remove the explosives from the vehicle before separating the vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove the explosives from the vehicle before separating the vehicles.
questions.explanation: In a collision, warn others of the danger and keep people away. Do not allow smoking or open fires near the vehicle. Before separating the vehicles, remove all explosives and place them at least 200 feet away from the vehicles and any buildings.

questions.question: ____ warn others about hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs called placards are placed on packages and the outside of vehicles to warn about hazardous materials. The shipper is responsible for placing the correct placards. The driver must verify they are correct.

questions.question: When transporting explosives, you must:
questions.explanation: You must follow a written route plan when transporting Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives. Avoid heavily populated areas, crowds, tunnels, narrow streets, and alleys. Check for any route restrictions before you drive.

questions.question: Hazardous materials placards are usually shaped like:
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: When transporting radioactive materials, you should know that:

options.text: Radiation will pass through to other packages.
The package should be placed in the cab.
The package should be loaded on its side.
The package should be made of wood.

questions.correctAnswerText: Radiation will pass through to other packages.
questions.explanation: Radiation passes through each package and reaches nearby packages. The number of packages that can be loaded together is limited.

questions.question: Who identifies the hazard class of materials being shipped?
questions.explanation: The shipper is responsible for identifying the hazard class and other details of hazardous materials, including the product number, shipping name, packing group, and correct packaging, labels, marking, and placards.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, do not park within 300 feet of:
questions.explanation: Never park a vehicle carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, or building, except for brief stops to refuel or perform necessary vehicle maintenance. Never park within five feet of the road. Park only briefly.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1 explosives, you must park at least ____ away from the nearest building.
questions.explanation: Do not park within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, or building when carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives. The only exception is brief stops for necessary operations, like refueling.

questions.question: A driver needs ____ to accept a package unless it looks clearly unsafe.
questions.explanation: Shippers must certify that hazardous materials are packaged correctly according to regulations. You can accept a package based on the shipper's certification unless it looks clearly unsafe or does not follow regulations.

questions.question: If a package is too small for a HazMat label, materials should be labeled:

options.text: With a piece of orange tape.

questions.explanation: If a hazardous materials package is too small for a label, attach the label to a tag. Fasten the tag securely to the package.

questions.question: Column 2 of the Hazardous Materials Table shows:
questions.explanation: Column 2 of the Hazardous Materials Table lists the proper shipping names and descriptions of regulated materials.

questions.question: If cargo is leaking, you should:

options.text: Touch the leaking material to identify the cargo.
Use shipping papers and labels to identify the leaking cargo.
Assume all the cargo is leaking.
Spray the leaking containers with water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use shipping papers and labels to identify the leaking cargo.
questions.explanation: If you find a leak in hazardous materials, identify the materials using the shipping papers, labels, or package location. Do not touch the leaking material.

questions.question: A person supervising the loading of a tank:

options.text: Does not need to know the materials being loaded.
Must be within 25 feet of the tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must be within 25 feet of the tank.
questions.explanation: A qualified person must watch the loading of hazardous materials into a tank. This person must stay alert and within 25 feet of the tank, have a clear view of it, know the hazards of the materials, know what to do in an emergency, and be able to move the tank if needed.

questions.question: Load hazardous materials:
questions.explanation: Always load hazardous materials away from heat sources. Heat can make many materials more dangerous.

questions.question: Do not smoke within ____ of a vehicle with placards for Class 3 or Division 2.1 materials.
questions.explanation: Do not smoke within 25 feet of a placarded tank carrying Class 3 (flammable liquids) or Division 2.1 (gases) materials. Also do not smoke within 25 feet of vehicles carrying Class 1 (explosives), Class 4 (flammable solids), or Class 4.2 (spontaneously combustible) materials.

questions.question: During a cargo fire, opening the trailer doors may cause the fire to expand because:

options.text: The temperature of the trailer changes.

questions.explanation: Opening trailer doors during a cargo fire allows oxygen to enter. This can cause the fire to flare up and spread.

questions.question: What is a clue that a shipment may contain hazardous materials?

options.text: The shipper is a business that typically handles hazardous materials.
The last shipment you picked up was labeled as hazardous.
The road is made of gravel.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipper is a business that typically handles hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: A clue that a shipment may contain hazardous materials is if the shipper is a business that works with them. Examples include paint dealers, chemical suppliers, pest control companies, agricultural suppliers, and dealers in explosives or fireworks.

questions.question: To transport hazardous materials, a driver needs:

options.text: A CDL with hazardous materials endorsement.
A CDL with a tank endorsement.

questions.correctAnswerText: A CDL with hazardous materials endorsement.
questions.explanation: To drive any vehicle that transports hazardous materials, you must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.

questions.question: If cargo with hazardous materials is leaking, what should the driver do?

options.text: Drive to find a phone and alert emergency personnel
Drive to a hazardous materials cleanup facility
Park the vehicle and contact emergency personnel

questions.correctAnswerText: Park the vehicle and contact emergency personnel
questions.explanation: When hazardous materials leak, stop driving immediately. Continuing to drive spreads contamination over a larger area. Park the vehicle, secure the area, stay with it, and send someone to get help.

questions.question: When transporting explosives, where can you leave your vehicle unattended?
questions.explanation: You can only leave a vehicle loaded with explosives unattended at an approved safe haven. A safe haven is a location approved for parking vehicles carrying explosives.

questions.question: When refueling a vehicle carrying hazardous materials, what must you do?
questions.explanation: Always turn off the engine before refueling a vehicle carrying hazardous materials. Someone must always be at the nozzle controlling fuel flow.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with empty hazardous materials tanks over railroad tracks, what must you do?

options.text: Stop at railroad crossings before proceeding

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at railroad crossings before proceeding
questions.explanation: You must always stop at railroad crossings before crossing, even if the hazardous materials tanks are empty.

questions.question: If hazardous material cargo catches fire, what should you do?

options.text: Try to put out the fire with a fire extinguisher
Contact emergency personnel and let them handle the fire
Continue driving to the fire department

questions.correctAnswerText: Contact emergency personnel and let them handle the fire
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials fires need specialized training and equipment to fight. Call emergency personnel and let them battle the fire.

questions.question: How should you check tire pressure?
questions.explanation: Check each tire before starting a trip. A tire pressure gauge is the only effective way to check tire pressure.

questions.question: What must be in the vehicle when transporting chlorine?
questions.explanation: A driver transporting chlorine must have an approved gas mask and an emergency kit in the vehicle for controlling leaks in cargo tank fittings.

questions.question: When loading compressed gas, the liquid discharge valves should be:
questions.explanation: Keep liquid discharge valves closed except when loading or unloading compressed gas.

questions.question: How should shipping papers be placed in the vehicle?

options.text: Easily seen by anyone entering the cab

questions.correctAnswerText: Easily seen by anyone entering the cab
questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers in a pouch on the driver's side door or where you can reach them with your seat belt on. They must be visible to anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: Class 1, Class 2.1, and Class 3 items should not be placed in a trailer with:
questions.explanation: Do not use cargo heaters when transporting Class 1 (Explosives), Class 2.1 (Flammable Gas), or Class 3 (Flammable Liquids) materials.
